method: C++ host controller tests; standalone PlatformIO ESP-IDF build; node --test web/tests/*.test.mjs (32tests); Python HTTP-handler suite (3tests); independent source review; esptool previous-app backup, write_flash and verify_flash three images; real browser native WebMCP discovery and all seven tools; controlled same-wiring servo-free timeout comparison.
environment: Windows local, COM7 CH343 ESP32-S3 N16R8 68ee8f4b6048. Owner explicitly confirmed all servos physically disconnected and V+OFF and authorized agent testing through localhost. Same four DuPont wires retained throughout comparison. Native document.modelContext on127.0.0.1:8765; no external MCP server or added dependency.
limitations: No physical waveform, current, motor load, end-stop or mechanical acceptance. S45 remains inconclusive; successful unloaded register traffic is not servo acceptance.
Power remains unknown to software. Servo-free/V+OFF are trusted owner reports, not measured by MCP.
IDF6.1 synchronous transaction code maps non-DONE status, including timeout, to0x108; logged INVALID_RESPONSE alone does not uniquely prove NACK.
A limited same-wiring comparison does not prove the root cause. Cable/contact integrity and repeated loaded behavior remain to be established.

Seven synchronous reads use configured20ms timeout/two100Hz ticks; internal waits/scheduling add latency and UARTStop is not serviced during sampling. Software500ms deadline is not a hard power cutoff.
MCP connect can lose its initial Stop during ESP boot and honestly returns an error; a separate explicit MCPStop establishes baseline. No motion retries or queued actions.
User requested testing before PR. PR207 remains closed unmerged; new source and receipts remain local pending the hardware test.
